title: reading notes - llm evals & inference tradeoffs
summary: Notes from papers, blog posts, and recent infra experiments focused on evaluation methodology and practical inference tradeoffs (latency, cost, quantization, fallback models). Prioritize ideas to test in Redwood serving runtime: prefix caching, AWQ vs GPTQ tradeoffs, evaluation metrics beyond perplexity.
content:
Quick context:
- Goal: collate readings + small experiments to inform inference recommendations for Redwood Optimize and serving runtime. Focus on evaluation that maps to production economics (latency, cost per token, failure modes).

Key papers / takeaways:
1) FlashAttention / FlashAttention2 (performance primitives) - arXiv: optimized kernels matter; significant speedups on longer sequences. Takeaway: measure end-to-end latency on realistic seq-lens, not just FLOPs.
2) QLoRA / AWQ / GPTQ notes - quantization landscape is messy:
   - QLoRA shows low-rank adapters allow finetuning with 4-bit weights. Good for fine-tuning but not necessarily for runtime-only inference.
   - AWQ claims better 3/4-bit integer post-training quant with minimal degradation on many tasks.
   - GPTQ still strong baseline; implementation and per-layer tuning matters.
   - Takeaway: run AWQ vs GPTQ cost/latency/quality A/B on 7B/13B models for our token distributions; record per-token latency and tail percentiles.
3) Eval metrics beyond perplexity: ROUGE/BLEU limited. Use training-free metrics + targeted prompts. Recommendations:
   - Use Likert-style scoring on a stratified prompt set (short/long, code, instruction-following).
   - Track hallucination via factuality checks (external API or knowledge-grounded tests).
   - Quantify latency-quality tradeoff: define quality loss threshold (e.g., <2% degrade) and measure cost savings.
4) Model fallbacks and routing policy research papers/blogs:
   - Multi-tier serving: small low-cost model for short queries, larger model for long/complex ones. Must detect routing cost-benefit on 95th percentile latency.
   - Investigate confidence-estimation heuristics for fallback decisions (logit margin, CE threshold).

Unresolved questions / experiments to run (priority order):
- Experiment A: AWQ vs GPTQ on Llama2-13B (our real prompt mix). Metrics: 50/90/99 latency, tokens/sec, quality on eval set (BLEU-like + instruction adherence).
- Experiment B: Prefix/KV caching effect on throughput for interactive chat workloads. Synthetic vs production traces. Hypothesis: caching yields 30-60% token cost reduction for highly conversational workloads.
- Experiment C: Service-level routing policy sim: 3-tier models, simulate traffic with our latency SLO and cost model. Measure percent requests served by each tier and SLA violations.

Practical notes from infra blog posts and talks:
- Measure end-to-end: serialization, network, and deserialization add non-trivial latency; kernel speedups only show when bytes in/out are accounted for.
- Batch sizes: dynamic batching helps throughput but hurts P95. Need fine-grained autoscaling + fast preemption.
- Quantized kernels sometimes have higher memory bandwidth; benchmark on the exact HW (A100 vs H100 vs older).

Quick checklist for next week (actionable):
- Spike: AWQ/GPTQ conversion script and baseline quality test on 1000 prompts (owner: Evelyn).
- Add a small eval harness that tracks cost per token and tail latency (owner: Marco).
- Draft a one-pager for Optimize team summarizing recommended rolling experiments and what telemetry we need from Console (owner: Samira).

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- When comparing quantized models, include failure cases (weird tokenization or numerical instabilities) in the eval set.
- Consider adding a small reward-model style evaluator for instruction adherence 	6 cheap proxy rather than full human evals.
- Keep a ledger of exact conversion flags used for each quant method (seed, per-channel scales, group size).

References (quick links):
- FlashAttention: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135
- GPTQ: https://github.com/IST-DASLab/gptq
- AWQ repo/blog: https://github.com/some-awq-repo (placeholder to replace with canonical link)

End.
